title: Status and handoff
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for answering what is done, what is next and where to resume, with evidence: read-only snapshots, status reports where done means verified, independent rechecks of claims, ranked next steps, handoffs when a session stops and resuming without trusting stale claims.
boundaries: Snapshots and rechecks only read; they change no repository, deployment or worker.
Done means verified with evidence. A claim from another worker or session counts as reported until a different worker rechecks it.
Failures and unknowns stay in every status; nothing is rounded up.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for answering what is done, what is next and where to resume, with evidence

value.lets_workers: Observe the real state of repositories, checks, deployments and workers; write a status where every item has a level and the evidence that level needs; have a different worker recheck claims; rank next steps with the person's decisions kept short; write a handoff when a session ends; and resume from a handoff by rechecking its claims before trusting them.

flow.when: Before any status, and first thing when resuming.
When someone asks what is done or open, and at every checkpoint.
For claims reported by another worker or session, before they count as done.
After a status, or when asked what is next.
Before a session stops for any reason, including a usage or context limit.
When a worker or session picks up someone else's work.

guardrails: Done means verified with evidence; anything else says what it is.
A claim from another session is a claim until rechecked.
Failures and unknowns stay in the status; nothing is rounded up.

nouns.title: How status, next steps and handoffs stay true
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: take-snapshot reads the current state from its sources, read-only.
write-status places every item at one level with the evidence that level needs.
recheck-claims has a different worker confirm or contradict reported claims.
rank-next-steps orders the work and keeps the person's list to three items.
write-handoff records ownership, next steps, open questions and claims to recheck.
resume-from-handoff rechecks those claims and looks for concurrent work before continuing.
rules: One status noun per checkpoint; never overwrite an earlier one.
Separate what was observed from what was reported, and date both.
A status answers in counts first, then the items that need the person.
Stopping without a handoff is a finding.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

nouns.title: Seven status levels and the evidence each needs

levels.means: Checked by a named worker with evidence of the right type.
Someone says it is done; nobody has rechecked it here.
levels.needs: claimed_by, claimed_at and how to recheck

levels.means: A named owner is working on it.
It cannot move without an answer, a credential, money, other work or an outside party.
It was tried and did not work; it stays on the record.
levels.needs: evidence and where it is kept

levels.means: Its state could not be read.

nouns.title: Which evidence supports which claim, and when it goes stale
nouns.category_reason: Deterministic matching of claims to evidence types and ages.

claim_to_evidence.checks passed: ci_run that ran on the exact head
claim_to_evidence.live: deployed_version with a matching digest from a parity check
claim_to_evidence.tested: test_run with the command, the counts and the exit code
claim_to_evidence.reviewed: review by a worker other than the author
claim_to_evidence.link works: link_check with the final address and status

value.rule: Evidence older than its maximum age is rechecked before a status relies on it; if it cannot be, the item is unknown, not done.

nouns.title: How next steps are ranked
nouns.category_reason: A deterministic ordering with stated tie-breaks.

order: Items with high deadline risk first.
Then items that unblock the most other items.
Then items whose evidence is going stale.
Then small items before large ones of equal value.
value.person_list: At most three items need the person, each as one decision with a recommended default.
value.never: Never rank a step that needs spending, credentials or a public release as a worker step.

nouns.title: Resuming after a usage limit, a context limit, a crash or a reassignment
nouns.category_reason: A recovery procedure for interrupted work.

steps: Read the latest handoff and the status report it points to.
Take a fresh snapshot; compare heads, checks and deployments with the handoff.
Recheck every claim the handoff lists, and every done_reported item you will build on.
Look for concurrent work: branches, locks and workers named in do_not_touch or seen in the snapshot.
Decide continue, continue with changes, or stop and ask; write that decision down before the first edit.
value.if_no_handoff: Treat the earlier session's claims as unknown, record a finding that it stopped without a handoff, and rebuild the status from a snapshot.

nouns.title: Template: a read-only observation of repositories, checks, deployments and workers at one time
nouns.category_reason: A snapshot is a recorded observation run.

value.describes: a read-only observation of repositories, checks, deployments and workers at one time
rules: Every value was read, not remembered.
Sources that could not be read are listed in unread.

nouns.title: Template: a status: every item at one level with the evidence that level needs, counts first
nouns.category_reason: A status report is a recorded assessment against evidence.

value.describes: a status: every item at one level with the evidence that level needs, counts first
rules: The headline gives counts and never says everything is done.
needs_person holds at most three decisions.

nouns.title: Template: a recheck of reported claims by a worker other than the claimant
nouns.category_reason: A claim check is a recorded verification run.

value.describes: a recheck of reported claims by a worker other than the claimant
rules: The checker is not the claimant.

nouns.title: Template: ranked next steps with their outcome, authority, effort and what they unblock
nouns.category_reason: A ranking is a proposal about what to do next.

value.describes: ranked next steps with their outcome, authority, effort and what they unblock
rules: Steps needing the person are authority person and appear in needs_person.

nouns.title: Template: a handoff: what the receiver owns, what to leave alone, next steps, open questions and claims to recheck
nouns.category_reason: A handoff is a claim about the state of work that the receiver must check.

value.describes: a handoff: what the receiver owns, what to leave alone, next steps, open questions and claims to recheck
rules: Every next step has a first check that proves the state before any edit.
Claims not rechecked before stopping are listed.

nouns.title: Template: the checks made when resuming from a handoff, and the decision that followed
nouns.category_reason: A resume check is a recorded verification run.

value.describes: the checks made when resuming from a handoff, and the decision that followed
rules: stop_and_ask when a claim is contradicted and the fix needs the person.
A conflict with concurrent work stops the resume.

nouns.title: Record checks for status reports, with synthetic golden reports
nouns.category_reason: A deterministic check suite with known-good and known-bad examples; the validator recomputes every verdict.

value.purpose: Checks every status report must pass before anyone relies on it. The two synthetic good reports pass all of them; each synthetic bad report fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: A status is true only as of a time.
The headline states counts, starting from what is verified.
A headline never says everything is done; it says how many items are verified.
Verified means a named check with evidence.
A claim not yet rechecked says who made it and when.
A blocked item carries the one question that unblocks it.
Failures stay on the record with their evidence.
An unknown says what would resolve it.
Every status ends with at least one owned next step.
Every fact comes from a dated source.

verbs.title: Take a snapshot of the current state
verbs.summary: Read the current heads, check runs, deployments and worker states for a named scope, without changing anything.
verbs.outcome: A snapshot with every value read at one time, and the sources that could not be read.

scope.description: Which repositories, deployments and workers to read.

steps: Read each value from its source at this time; never copy a value from an earlier status.
Record heads as full or short commit identifiers and check runs with the head they ran on.
List every source that could not be read in unread instead of guessing its state.

acceptance.check: The snapshot validates against template.snapshot's schema.
Every repository, deployment and worker named in scope appears either with its values or in unread.

network: Read-only requests to the code host's API and the named deployments' health and version pages; nothing is changed.
capabilities: read-only access to the named repositories and deployments
write candidate nouns in the requester's scope

verbs.title: Write an evidence-backed status
verbs.summary: Place every item in scope at one status level with the evidence that level needs, and lead with counts.
verbs.outcome: A status report that passes the status checks.

slots.name: earlier_reports
slots.description: Pins of earlier status reports, handoffs or receipts.

steps: Start from the snapshot. Carry an earlier claim forward only as done_reported, with who made it and when.
Mark an item done_verified only with evidence of the type the evidence rules name, younger than its maximum age.
Keep failures and unknowns; give each failure its evidence and each unknown what would resolve it.
Write the headline as counts by level, verified first.
Put at most three decisions in needs_person, each answerable in one line.

acceptance.check: The report validates against template.status-report's schema.
The report passes the pinned status checks.
The headline's counts equal the lengths of the level lists.

verbs.title: Recheck reported claims
verbs.summary: A worker other than the claimant rechecks each done_reported claim, and samples verified ones, against fresh evidence.
verbs.outcome: A claim check: each claim confirmed, contradicted or unverifiable, with evidence.

slots.name: status_report
slots.description: Pin of the status report whose claims to recheck.

steps: Confirm you made none of the claims you check; otherwise end blocked.
Recheck each claim with the evidence type the rules name, read now.
Mark a claim contradicted only with evidence; mark it unverifiable when the evidence cannot be read.
Propose record-finding for every contradicted claim.

acceptance.check: The claim check validates against template.claim-check's schema.
Every done_reported item in the report appears in claims.

network: Read-only requests to the code host's API and the deployed pages named in the claims; nothing is changed.

verbs.title: Rank the next steps
verbs.summary: Turn a status into ranked next steps, each a verb with an outcome, authority, effort and what it unblocks.
verbs.outcome: Ranked next steps, with at most three items for the person.
steps: Apply the ranking rules in order and say which rule decided each tie.
Give every step a verb kind and an outcome another worker could check.
Mark steps that need spending, credentials or a public release as authority person; keep them to three.

acceptance.check: The ranking validates against template.next-steps's schema.
Every blocked item in the status appears as a step or in needs_person.
A reviewer agrees the first step is the most valuable one available now.

verbs.title: Write a handoff
verbs.summary: Before a session stops, record what the receiver owns, what to leave alone, the next steps with a first check each, open questions and unchecked claims.
verbs.outcome: A handoff another worker can resume from without asking.

slots.name: status_report
slots.description: Pin of the latest status report.

steps: Write the handoff before the session stops; a handoff written late misses claims.
List what the receiver owns and what others own, by branch, file or noun.
Give each next step a first check that proves the state before any edit.
List every claim you did not recheck, plainly.

acceptance.check: The handoff validates against template.handoff's schema.
status_report_ref names the pinned status report.
A different worker could take the first step using only this handoff and its pins.

verbs.title: Resume from a handoff
verbs.summary: Pick up someone else's work by rechecking the handoff's claims, looking for concurrent work and deciding whether to continue.
verbs.outcome: A resume check with the decision and the first step.

slots.name: snapshot
slots.description: Pin of a snapshot taken after the handoff was written.

steps: Compare the fresh snapshot with the handoff: heads, checks, deployments and workers.
Recheck every claim the handoff lists before building on it.
Leave anything in do_not_touch alone; a conflict with concurrent work means stop_and_ask.
Write the decision and the first step before making any change.

acceptance.check: The resume check validates against template.resume-check's schema.
Every claim in claims_to_recheck appears in claims.
decision is stop_and_ask whenever concurrent_work holds a conflict.
